title.raw: 卷二十 列傳第十 謝弘微 Volume 20 Biographies 10: Xie Hongwei

sentences.zh: 列傳第十

translations.literal: Biographies 10
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 10

sentences.zh: 謝弘微

translations.literal: Xie Hongwei
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hongwei

sentences.zh: 谢密，字弘微，晋西中郎万之曾孙、尚书左僕射景仁从子也。

translations.literal: Xie Mi, styled Hongwei, was great-grandson of Wan, Western General of the Household under Jin, and nephew of Jingren, Vice Director of the Left Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Mi, courtesy name Hongwei, was great-grandson of Wan, Western General of the Household under Jin, and nephew of Jingren, Vice Director of the Left Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 祖韶，车骑司马。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao served as Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 父思，武昌太守。

translations.literal: His father Si was Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Si held office as Administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 弘微年十歲，繼從叔峻，名犯所繼內諱，故以字行。

translations.literal: Hongwei at age ten succeeded to his father's younger cousin Jun; his personal name violated the taboo of the family he succeeded into, so he went by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: At ten, Hongwei was adopted by his father's younger cousin Jun; since his personal name clashed with the taboo name of his adoptive kin, he made himself known by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 童幼時精神端審，時然後言。

translations.literal: In childhood his spirit was upright and careful; he spoke only when the occasion was right.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was composed and earnest, and spoke only when the moment called for it.

sentences.zh: 所繼叔父混名知人，見而異之，謂思曰：「此兒深中夙敏，方成佳器，有子如此足矣。

translations.literal: His adoptive uncle Hun, famed for knowing men, saw him and was struck; he said to Si, "This boy is inwardly gifted and precocious from youth; he will become fine material—with such a son, one has enough."
translations.idiomatic: His adoptive uncle Hun, renowned for reading character, saw him and marveled; he told Si, "This child carries deep native wit and early brilliance; he will become a vessel of worth. To have such a son is enough."

sentences.zh: 」峻司空琰子也，於弘微本服緦，親戚中表，素不相識，率意承接，皆合禮衷。

translations.literal: Jun was son of Yan, Minister of Works; to Hongwei he was originally only a distant kinsman in mourning garb; among affinal and maternal relatives he had never known, yet he received them all as impulse directed, and every fit was within ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was the son of Yan, Minister of Works; to Hongwei he had been no more than a distant cousin in the coarsest mourning grade, and among affinal and maternal kin he had never met, yet he received each one as instinct prompted, and every response fell within the heart of ritual.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，襲爵建昌縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, he inherited the title Marquis of Jianchang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yixi era he inherited the title Marquis of Jianchang County.

sentences.zh: 弘微家素貧儉，而所繼豐泰，唯受數千卷書，國吏數人而已，遺財祿秩，一不關預。

translations.literal: Hongwei's family had always been poor and frugal, while the household he succeeded to was rich and prosperous; he accepted only several thousand scrolls of books and a few dozen household officials, and had no part in inherited wealth, stipends, or ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei's birth family had always lived plainly, while the estate he inherited was lavish; he took only a few thousand scrolls of books and a handful of estate officers, and would not touch a coin of the inherited income or rank.

sentences.zh: 混聞而驚歎，謂國郎中令漆凱之曰：「建昌國祿本應與北舍共之，國侯既不厝意，今可依常分送。

translations.literal: Hun heard this and sighed in wonder; he told the estate's Chief Clerk Qi Kaizhi, "The income of the Jianchang fief ought to be shared with the northern house; since the marquis shows no interest, send the usual allotment now."
translations.idiomatic: When Hun heard of this he sighed in astonishment and told the estate's Chief Clerk Qi Kaizhi, "The Jianchang fief income should be shared with the northern house; since the marquis wants none of it, send the usual share as before."

sentences.zh: 弘微重違混言，乃少有所受。

translations.literal: Hongwei, loath to go against Hun's words, then accepted a little.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to defy Hun outright, Hongwei accepted only a modest portion.

sentences.zh: 北舍，弘微本家也。

translations.literal: The northern house was Hongwei's original family.
translations.idiomatic: The northern house was Hongwei's birth family.

sentences.zh: 混風格高峻，少所交納，唯與族子靈運、瞻、晦、曜、弘微以文義賞會，常共宴處，居在烏衣巷，故謂之烏衣之遊。

translations.literal: Hun's manner was lofty and stern; he had few associates, and only with his clansmen Lingyun, Zhan, Hui, Yao, and Hongwei did he meet in literary fellowship, often feasting together; they lived in Wuyi Lane, and so their gatherings were called the Wuyi fellowship.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's bearing was lofty and austere, and he admitted few companions; only with his kinsmen Lingyun, Zhan, Hui, Yao, and Hongwei did he gather for literary conversation, often feasting together in Wuyi Lane—hence the name the Wuyi fellowship.

sentences.zh: 混詩所言：「昔為烏衣游，戚戚皆親姓。

translations.literal: What Hun's poem says: "Once we roamed Wuyi Lane, kin all close at hand."
translations.idiomatic: This is what Hun meant in his poem: "Once we roamed Wuyi Lane, kin all close at hand."

sentences.zh: 」者也。

translations.literal: —so it runs.
translations.idiomatic: —so the line goes.

sentences.zh: 其外雖復高流時譽，莫敢造門。

translations.literal: Though eminent men of the age and men of repute existed beyond them, none dared knock at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: However celebrated the eminent men of the day, none ventured to call at his door.

sentences.zh: 瞻等才辭辯富，弘微每以約言服之，混特所敬貴，號曰微子。

translations.literal: Zhan and the others were rich in talent and eloquence; Hongwei always won them over with brief words; Hun especially honored him and called him Master Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and the others were gifted and eloquent, yet Hongwei always subdued them with spare speech; Hun held him in special esteem and styled him Master Wei.

sentences.zh: 謂瞻等曰：「汝諸人雖才義豐辯，未必皆愜眾心，至於領會機賞，言約理要，故當與我共推微子。

translations.literal: He told Zhan and the others, "You all may be rich in talent and righteousness and fluent in debate, yet you may not all satisfy the hearts of the crowd; as for grasping the moment and judging merit, speaking little yet hitting the point—there you should join me in elevating Master Wei."
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhan and the others, "You may be rich in talent and fluent in debate, yet not all of you win every heart; when it comes to reading the moment and weighing merit in few words and to the point, you should join me in holding up Master Wei."

sentences.zh: 常言：「阿遠剛躁負氣，阿客博而無檢，曜仗才而持操不篤，晦自知而納善不周。

translations.literal: He often said, "A Yuan is rash and hot-tempered, A Ke is broad but unrestrained, Yao relies on talent yet holds to principle without steadiness, Hui knows himself yet takes in good counsel without completeness."
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "A Yuan is brash and proud, A Ke is learned but undisciplined, Yao has talent yet lacks constancy, and Hui knows himself yet does not fully embrace what is good."

sentences.zh: 設復功濟三才，終亦以此為恨。

translations.literal: Even if their achievements matched the Three Talents, in the end they would regret this.
translations.idiomatic: Even were their deeds to equal the Three Talents, they would still rue these faults in the end.

sentences.zh: 至如微子，吾無間然」。

translations.literal: As for Master Wei, I find no fault in him."
translations.idiomatic: As for Master Wei, I find no fault in him."

sentences.zh: 又言：「微子異不傷物，同不害正，若年造六十，必至公輔」。

translations.literal: He also said, "Master Wei differs without harming others, agrees without harming what is right; if he reaches sixty, he will surely rise to minister and aide."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Master Wei stands apart without wounding others and joins in without compromising principle; should he live to sixty, he will surely reach the highest offices."

sentences.zh: 嘗因酣燕之余，為韻語以獎勸靈運、瞻等曰：「康樂誕通度，實有名家韻，若加繩染功，剖瑩乃瓊瑾。

translations.literal: Once, amid the ease of a feast, he composed rhymed lines to encourage Lingyun, Zhan, and the others, saying, "Kangle was born with far-reaching grace, truly bearing the tone of a great house; add the work of the finishing dye, split the crystal and it becomes jade."
translations.idiomatic: Once, after wine had loosened the mood, he composed rhymed verses to exhort Lingyun, Zhan, and the rest: "Kangle was born with a patrician air, truly the measure of a great clan; add the polish of the final dye, and split the stone to reveal jade."

sentences.zh: 宣明體遠識，穎達且沈俊，若能去方執，穆穆三才順。

translations.literal: Xuanming's bearing holds far sight, keen and penetrating yet deep and handsome; if he can leave obstinacy behind, the Three Talents will accord in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanming's mind reaches far, keen yet deep and refined; if he can cast off stubbornness, heaven, earth, and man will move in harmony.

sentences.zh: 阿多標獨解，弱冠纂華胤，質勝誡無文，其尚又能峻。

translations.literal: A Duo stands alone in insight, at twenty inheriting splendid lineage; substance surpassing ornament warns against lack of polish, yet his aspirations can still be lofty.
translations.idiomatic: A Duo stands apart in insight, at twenty inheriting a splendid line; where substance outruns ornament one must guard against roughness, yet his aims can still be stern.

sentences.zh: 通遠懷清悟，采采摽蘭訊，直轡鮮不躓，抑用解偏吝。

translations.literal: Tongyuan cherishes clear understanding, picking orchid messages again and again; a straight rein rarely fails to stumble—restrain it and partial stinginess will ease.
translations.idiomatic: Tongyuan holds to lucid insight, gathering orchid tidings again and again; the straight rein seldom avoids a stumble—check it, and petty reluctance will loosen.

sentences.zh: 微子基微尚，無倦由慕藺，勿輕一簣少，進往必千仞。

translations.literal: Master Wei bases himself on modest aspiration; tireless because he emulates Lin, do not slight one basket's shortfall—the advance ahead must reach a thousand fathoms.
translations.idiomatic: Master Wei rests on modest aims, untiring because he emulates Lin; do not despise one basket's shortfall, for the climb ahead must reach a thousand fathoms.

sentences.zh: 數子勉之哉，風流由爾振。

translations.literal: You sons, strive on—the current of elegance will be renewed through you.
translations.idiomatic: Strive on, all of you—the age's refinement will be renewed through you.

sentences.zh: 如不犯所知，此外無所慎。

translations.literal: If you do not offend those you know, beyond that there is nothing to guard against."
translations.idiomatic: So long as you give no offense to those who know you, nothing else need be feared."

sentences.zh: 」靈運、瞻等並有誡厲之言，唯弘微獨盡褒美。

translations.literal: Lingyun, Zhan, and the others all received admonitory words; only Hongwei received unmixed praise.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun, Zhan, and the others all received words of warning; Hongwei alone was praised without reserve.

sentences.zh: 曜，弘微兄，多其小字。

translations.literal: Yao was Hongwei's elder brother; Duo was his childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was Hongwei's elder brother; Duo was his childhood name.

sentences.zh: 通遠即瞻字。

translations.literal: Tongyuan was Zhan's courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Tongyuan was Zhan's courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 客兒，靈運小名也。

translations.literal: Ke'er was Lingyun's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Ke'er was Lingyun's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 晉世名家身有國封者，起家多拜員外散騎侍郎，弘微亦拜員外散騎侍郎、琅邪王大司馬參軍。

translations.literal: In the Jin age, when men of great houses held state fiefs, they usually began office as Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; Hongwei also received appointment as Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal of Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, scions of great houses with state fiefs usually entered service as Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; Hongwei received the same appointment and became Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal of the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，混以劉毅黨見誅，混妻晉陵公主改適琅邪王練。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as a partisan of Liu Yi; Hun's wife, the Princess of Jinling, was remarried to Prince Lian of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as an ally of Liu Yi; Hun's wife, the Princess of Jinling, was ordered to remarry Prince Lian of Langye.

sentences.zh: 公主雖執意不行，而詔與謝氏離絕。

translations.literal: Though the princess firmly refused, an edict severed her from the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Though the princess steadfastly refused, an edict cut her ties to the Xie house.

sentences.zh: 公主以混家事委之弘微。

translations.literal: The princess entrusted the Hun household affairs to Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: The princess placed the Hun household in Hongwei's hands.

sentences.zh: 混仍世宰相，一門兩封，田業十餘處，僮役千人，唯有二女，年並數歲。

translations.literal: Hun's family for generations had held the chancellorship; one gate held two fiefs; fields and estates numbered more than ten; servants and retainers reached a thousand; he had only two daughters, both only a few years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Hun line had produced chancellors for generations; one household held two fiefs, more than ten estates, and a thousand servants and retainers, with only two daughters, each still only a few years old.

sentences.zh: 弘微經紀生業，事若在公，一錢尺帛出入，皆有文簿。

translations.literal: Hongwei managed the livelihood as though it were public business; every coin or foot of cloth in or out had written records.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei managed the estate as if it were public office; every coin and every foot of cloth that passed in or out went into written ledgers.

sentences.zh: 宋武受命，晉陵公主降封東鄉君。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song received the Mandate, the Princess of Jinling was demoted to Lady of Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song took the throne, the Princess of Jinling was reduced in rank to Lady of Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 以混得罪前代，東鄉君節義可嘉，聽還謝氏。

translations.literal: Because Hun had been condemned by the previous dynasty, yet Lady Dongxiang's integrity was commendable, she was permitted to return to the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hun had been condemned under the previous dynasty, Lady Dongxiang's constancy was judged worthy, and she was allowed to rejoin the Xie house.

sentences.zh: 自混亡至是九年，而室宇修整，倉廩充盈，門徒不異平日。

translations.literal: From Hun's death until then was nine years, yet the halls were repaired, the granaries full, and the household staff unchanged from ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years had passed since Hun's death, yet the halls stood in good repair, the granaries were full, and the household staff looked no different from ordinary days.

sentences.zh: 田疇墾辟，有加於舊。

translations.literal: Fields were opened to cultivation and exceeded what had been before.
translations.idiomatic: The fields had been cleared and brought under the plow, surpassing what they had been before.

sentences.zh: 東鄉君歎曰：「僕射生平重此子，可謂知人，僕射為不亡矣。

translations.literal: Lady Dongxiang sighed and said, "The Vice Director in his lifetime valued this boy; one may say he knew men—the Vice Director is not dead."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Dongxiang sighed and said, "In life the Vice Director prized this boy; he truly knew men—the Vice Director lives on in him."

sentences.zh: 」中外姻親、道俗義舊見東鄉之歸者，入門莫不歎息，或為流涕，感弘微之義也。

translations.literal: Affinal kin within and without, monks and lay friends who had known Lady Dongxiang—everyone who saw her return entered the gate sighing, some weeping, moved by Hongwei's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen near and far, monks and old friends who had known Lady Dongxiang—everyone who saw her return sighed at the threshold, some in tears, stirred by Hongwei's devotion.

sentences.zh: 性嚴正，舉止必循禮度，事繼親之黨，恭謹過常。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and upright; in bearing he always followed ritual measure; toward the kin of his adoptive family he was more deferential than custom required.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern and upright by nature, measured his every move by ritual, and toward his adoptive kin showed a deference beyond ordinary duty.

sentences.zh: 伯叔二母，歸宗兩姑，晨夕瞻奉，盡其誠敬。

translations.literal: Two paternal aunts by marriage and two aunts who had returned to their natal houses—morning and evening he attended them with full sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Two paternal aunts by marriage and two aunts returned to their natal house—morning and evening he waited on them with complete devotion.

sentences.zh: 內外或傳語通訊，輒正其衣冠。

translations.literal: Within the household or when relaying messages from outside, he would straighten his cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Whether within the household or when messages came from outside, he would set his cap and robes in order.

sentences.zh: 婢僕之前，不妄言笑。

translations.literal: Before maids and servants he never spoke or laughed lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Before maids and servants he never spoke or laughed casually.

sentences.zh: 由是尊卑大小，敬之若神。

translations.literal: Because of this, high and low, great and small, revered him as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason everyone in the household, high and low, revered him as though he were sacred.

sentences.zh: 時有蔡湛之者，及見謝安兄弟，謂人曰：「弘微貌類中郎，而性似文靖。」

translations.literal: There was one Cai Zhizhi; when he saw the Xie An brothers he told others, "Hongwei's face resembles the Middle Commander, but his nature resembles Wenjing."
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Cai Zhizhi; after seeing the Xie An brothers he said to others, "Hongwei's face recalls the Middle Commander, but his character recalls Wenjing."

sentences.zh: 居身清約，器服不華，而飲食滋味盡其豐美。

translations.literal: In personal conduct he was plain and restrained; vessels and dress were not ornate, yet in food and drink he enjoyed every richness of flavor.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and without display; his utensils and dress were never showy, yet his table held every delicacy.

sentences.zh: 兄曜曆御史中丞，彭城王義康驃騎長史，卒官。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yao successively held the posts of Imperial Censor and Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General of Prince Kang of Pengcheng, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yao rose to Imperial Censor and Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General of Prince Kang of Pengcheng, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 弘微哀戚過禮，服雖除猶不噉魚肉。

translations.literal: Hongwei's grief exceeded ritual; though mourning garb was removed he still ate no fish or meat.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei mourned beyond what ritual required; even after the mourning period ended he still abstained from fish and meat.

sentences.zh: 沙門釋慧琳嘗與之食，見其猶蔬素，謂曰：「檀越素既多疾，即吉猶未復膳。

translations.literal: The monk Huilin once ate with him; seeing him still on vegetables he said, "Lay patron, you have long been ill; even after reaching the end of mourning you have not resumed a proper diet.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huilin once shared a meal with him; seeing him still on plain fare he said, "Lay patron, you have long been frail; even now that mourning is ended you have not returned to a proper diet.

sentences.zh: 若以無益傷生，豈所望於得理。

translations.literal: If harm to life brings no benefit, that is hardly what reason would hope for."
translations.idiomatic: If you injure your health to no good end, that can hardly be what reason demands."

sentences.zh: 」弘微曰：「衣冠之變，禮不可踰，在心之哀，實未能已。

translations.literal: Hongwei said, "The change of cap and robe—ritual cannot be overstepped; the grief within the heart truly cannot yet cease."
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei replied, "The change of cap and robe—ritual cannot be breached; the sorrow in my heart truly cannot yet be stilled."

sentences.zh: 」遂廢食歔欷不自勝。

translations.literal: He then stopped eating and sobbed beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Then he put aside his food and wept until he could not contain himself.

sentences.zh: 弘微少孤，事兄如父。

translations.literal: Hongwei was orphaned young and served his elder brother as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Hongwei served his elder brother as he would a father.

sentences.zh: 友睦之至，舉世莫及。

translations.literal: In brotherly harmony he surpassed all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In brotherly affection he had no equal under heaven.

sentences.zh: 口不言人短，見兄曜好臧否人物，每聞之，常亂以他語。

translations.literal: He never spoke of others' faults; seeing his brother Yao fond of judging people, whenever he heard it he would interrupt with other talk.
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke of others' faults; when he saw his brother Yao delight in passing judgment on people, he would break in with another subject.

sentences.zh: 歷位中庶子，加侍中。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Palace Companion and was additionally appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts to Palace Companion and was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 志在素宦，畏忌權寵，固讓不拜，乃聽解中庶子。

translations.literal: His ambition lay in plain office; he feared and shunned power and favor, firmly declined appointment, and was permitted to resign the post of Palace Companion.
translations.idiomatic: He sought only modest office, feared power and favor, firmly declined appointment, and was allowed to resign as Palace Companion.

sentences.zh: 每獻替及陳事，必手書焚草，人莫之知。

translations.literal: Whenever he offered remonstrance or presented business, he always wrote by hand and burned the draft; no one knew.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he remonstrated or submitted memorials, he wrote in his own hand and burned the draft, so no one ever knew.

sentences.zh: 上以弘微能膳羞，每就求食，弘微與親舊經營。

translations.literal: Because the Emperor knew Hongwei could prepare fine dishes, he often came to ask for food; Hongwei would prepare them with kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Hongwei could prepare fine dishes, the Emperor often came to request a meal; Hongwei would arrange them with kin and old friends.

sentences.zh: 及進之後，親人問上所禦，弘微不答，別以餘語酬之，時人比之漢世孔光。

translations.literal: After they were served, when kin asked what the Emperor had eaten, Hongwei would not answer and would reply with other words; people of the time compared him to Kong Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor had eaten, when kin asked what dishes had been served, Hongwei would not answer and turned the talk elsewhere; contemporaries compared him to Kong Guang of Han.

sentences.zh: 及東鄉君薨，遺財千萬，園宅十餘所，又會稽、吳興、琅邪諸處太傅安、司空琰時事業，奴僮猶數百人，公私咸謂室內資財宜歸二女，田宅僮僕應屬弘微，弘微一不取。

translations.literal: When Lady Dongxiang died, the estate left wealth of ten million, more than ten gardens and mansions, and moreover the enterprises of Grand Tutor An and Minister of Works Yan at Kuaiji, Wuxing, and Langye; slaves and servants still numbered several hundred; public and private opinion alike held that movable property should go to the two daughters while fields, houses, and servants should belong to Hongwei—Hongwei took none of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Dongxiang died, the estate held ten million in wealth, more than ten gardens and mansions, and the enterprises Grand Tutor An and Minister of Works Yan had held in Kuaiji, Wuxing, and Langye, with several hundred slaves and servants still on the rolls; everyone agreed movable property should go to the two daughters and land, houses, and retainers to Hongwei—Hongwei took nothing.

sentences.zh: 自以私祿營葬。

translations.literal: He paid for the burial from his private stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He covered the burial costs from his own salary.

sentences.zh: 混女夫殷叡素好摴蒱，聞弘微不取財物，乃濫奪其妻妹及伯母兩姑之分以還戲責，內人皆化弘微之讓，一無所爭。

translations.literal: Hun's son-in-law Yin Rui had always loved dice games; hearing Hongwei would take no property, he seized his wife's younger sister's share and the portions of the two paternal aunts to pay gambling debts; the women within all followed Hongwei's yielding example and contested nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's son-in-law Yin Rui was devoted to dice; learning Hongwei would accept no property, he seized his wife's younger sister's portion and the shares of the two paternal aunts to settle gambling debts; the women of the household, following Hongwei's example of yielding, raised no dispute.

sentences.zh: 弘微舅子領軍將軍劉湛謂弘微曰：「天下事宜有裁衷，卿此不問，何以居官？

translations.literal: Hongwei's nephew by marriage, General of the Guards Liu Zhan, said to Hongwei, "Affairs under heaven ought to have measured judgment—if you ask nothing about this, how can you hold office?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei's nephew by marriage, General of the Guards Liu Zhan, said to him, "Public affairs need measured judgment; if you refuse to intervene here, how can you hold office?"

sentences.zh: 」弘微笑而不答。

translations.literal: Hongwei smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei smiled and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 或有譏以「謝氏累世財產，充殷君一朝戲責，譬棄物江海以為廉耳」。

translations.literal: Some mocked him, saying, "The Xie clan's wealth accumulated over generations was consumed in one day by Lord Yin's gambling debts—as though casting goods into river and sea were called integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked him: "Wealth the Xie clan had built over generations was lost in a day to Lord Yin's gambling debts—as if throwing property into river and sea were the same as integrity."

sentences.zh: 弘微曰：「親戚爭財，為鄙之甚，今內人尚能無言，豈可導之使爭。

translations.literal: Hongwei said, "For kin to fight over wealth is the depth of vulgarity; now the women within can still keep silent—how could I lead them to quarrel?
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei said, "For kin to wrangle over wealth is the depth of vulgarity; the women of the house remain silent—how could I teach them to quarrel?

sentences.zh: 今分多共少，不至有乏，身死之後，豈復見關。」

translations.literal: Now if shares are many and shares few, there will be no want; after I am dead, what further concern can there be?"
translations.idiomatic: Whether the shares are large or small, none will go wanting; once I am dead, what further concern can there be?"

sentences.zh: 東鄉君葬，混墓開，弘微牽疾臨赴，病遂甚。

translations.literal: At Lady Dongxiang's burial, Hun's tomb was opened; Hongwei, dragging his illness, went to attend, and his illness grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: At Lady Dongxiang's burial Hun's tomb was opened; Hongwei dragged himself there despite illness, and his condition worsened sharply.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十年卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanjia he died, age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanjia he died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘆惜甚至，謂謝景仁曰：「謝弘微、王曇首年踰四十，名位未盡其才，此朕之責也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen grieved deeply and told Xie Jingren, "Xie Hongwei and Wang Tanshou passed forty, yet name and rank did not exhaust their talent—this is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen mourned him deeply and told Xie Jingren, "Xie Hongwei and Wang Tanshou were past forty, yet rank and title never matched their gifts—that fault is mine."

sentences.zh: 弘微性寬博，無喜慍。

translations.literal: Hongwei's nature was broad and tolerant; he showed neither joy nor anger.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei was broad-minded and even-tempered, showing neither joy nor anger.

sentences.zh: 末年嘗與友人棋，友人西南棋有死勢，復一客曰：「西南風急，或有覆舟者。

translations.literal: In his later years he once played weiqi with a friend; the friend's southwest position had a fatal shape, and another guest said, "The southwest wind is strong—perhaps a capsized boat."
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he once played weiqi with a friend; the friend's southwest cluster was doomed, and another guest said, "The southwest wind is rising—someone may capsize."

sentences.zh: 」友悟乃救之。

translations.literal: The friend understood and saved it.
translations.idiomatic: The friend caught the hint and saved the position.

sentences.zh: 弘微大怒，投局於地。

translations.literal: Hongwei grew greatly angry and threw the board to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei flared in anger and hurled the board to the floor.

sentences.zh: 識者知其暮年之事，果以此歲終。

translations.literal: Those who knew him understood that his last years were at hand; indeed he died that year.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew him saw that his end was near; he did die that same year.

sentences.zh: 時有一長鬼寄司馬文宣家，言被遣殺弘微。

translations.literal: At the time a tall ghost lodged in the house of Sima Wenxuan, saying it had been sent to kill Hongwei.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a tall ghost possessed the house of Sima Wenxuan, claiming it had been dispatched to kill Hongwei.

sentences.zh: 弘微疾每劇，輒豫告文宣。

translations.literal: Whenever Hongwei's illness grew acute, it would forewarn Wenxuan in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hongwei's illness worsened, the ghost warned Wenxuan beforehand.

sentences.zh: 及弘微死，與文宣分別而去。

translations.literal: When Hongwei died, it took leave of Wenxuan and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongwei died, it bade Wenxuan farewell and left.

sentences.zh: 弘微臨終語左右曰：「有二摎書，須劉領軍至，可於前燒之，慎勿開也。

translations.literal: At the end Hongwei told those beside him, "There are two sealed letters; wait until General Liu arrives, then burn them before him—take care not to open them."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Hongwei told his attendants, "There are two sealed letters; when General Liu comes, burn them in his presence—do not open them."

sentences.zh: 」書是文帝手敕，上甚痛惜之。

translations.literal: The letters were the Emperor Wen's own hand; the Emperor grieved deeply over them.
translations.idiomatic: The letters bore Emperor Wen's own hand; the Emperor mourned them bitterly.

sentences.zh: 使二衛千人營畢葬事，追贈太常。

translations.literal: He sent a thousand men of the Two Guards to complete the burial and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched a thousand men of the Two Guards to finish the burial and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 弘微與琅邪王惠、王球並以簡淡稱，人謂沈約曰：「王惠何如？

translations.literal: Hongwei, together with Wang Hui and Wang Qiu of Langye, were all known for plain detachment; people asked Shen Yue, "How is Wang Hui?"
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei, with Wang Hui and Wang Qiu of Langye, was famed for plain detachment; when people asked Shen Yue, "What of Wang Hui?"

sentences.zh: 」約曰：「令明簡。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Lingming is plain."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Lingming is spare."

sentences.zh: 」次問王球，約曰：「蒨玉淡。

translations.literal: Next they asked about Wang Qiu; Yue said, "Qianyu is detached."
translations.idiomatic: Asked next about Wang Qiu, Yue said, "Qianyu is coolly detached."

sentences.zh: 」又次問弘微，約曰：「簡而不失，淡而不流，古之所謂名臣，弘微當之。

translations.literal: Then they asked about Hongwei; Yue said, "Plain without loss, detached without drift—the minister of ancient fame; Hongwei fits the name."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Hongwei, Yue said, "Spare without losing substance, detached without losing hold—the sort of minister the ancients praised; Hongwei is that man."

sentences.zh: 」其見美如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he admired.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 子莊。

translations.literal: His son was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 莊字希逸，七歲能屬文，及長，韶令美容儀，宋文帝見而異之，謂尚書僕射殷景仁、領軍將軍劉湛曰：「藍田生玉，豈虛也哉。

translations.literal: Zhuang, styled Xiyi, at seven could compose prose; when grown, his bearing and mien were fine; Emperor Wen of Song saw him and was struck; he told Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yin Jingren and General of the Guards Liu Zhan, "A jade born in Lantian—can it be empty praise?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang, courtesy name Xiyi, could compose prose at seven; grown, he was handsome in bearing; Emperor Wen of Song saw him and marveled, telling Vice Director Yin Jingren and General of the Guards Liu Zhan, "Jade born in Lantian—is the praise empty?"

sentences.zh: 」為隨王誕後軍諮議，領記室。

translations.literal: He served as Rear Army Adviser to Prince Dan of Sui and headed the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Rear Army Adviser to Prince Dan of Sui and headed the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 分左氏經傳，隨國立篇。

translations.literal: He divided the Zuo Commentary and established chapters for the Sui principality.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the Zuo Commentary into sections and established chapters for the Sui principality.

sentences.zh: 制木方丈，圖山川土地，各有分理。

translations.literal: He made a wooden square one zhang on a side, mapping mountains, rivers, and lands, each with its proper division.
translations.idiomatic: He fashioned a wooden square one zhang on a side, charting mountains, rivers, and lands, each in its proper place.

sentences.zh: 離之則州郡殊別，合之則宇內為一。

translations.literal: Separated they showed each province and commandery distinct; joined they formed the realm within the Four Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Taken apart they showed each province and commandery; joined together they formed the realm within the Four Seas.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，魏攻彭城，遣尚書李孝伯與鎮軍長史張暢語，孝伯訪問莊及王微，其名聲遠布如此。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, when Wei attacked Pengcheng, the Emperor sent Minister of Writing Li Xiaobo to speak with Chief Clerk to the General Who Guards the Army Zhang Chang; Xiaobo inquired about Zhuang and Wang Wei—their fame had spread so far.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia twenty-seven, when Wei attacked Pengcheng, the court sent Minister of Writing Li Xiaobo to parley with Chief Clerk Zhang Chang of the Army of the General Who Guards the Army; Xiaobo asked after Zhuang and Wang Wei—their reputations had spread that widely.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，除太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Palace Companion.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Palace Companion.

sentences.zh: 時南平王鑠獻赤鸚鵡，普詔群臣為賦。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Shuo of Nanping presented a scarlet parrot; a general edict ordered the ministers to compose fu.
translations.idiomatic: Then Prince Shuo of Nanping presented a scarlet parrot, and an edict ordered the ministers to compose fu.

sentences.zh: 太子左衛率袁淑文冠當時，作賦畢示莊。

translations.literal: Left Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent Yuan Shu was foremost in letters of the age; when he finished his fu he showed it to Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent Yuan Shu led the age in letters; when he finished his fu he showed it to Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 及見莊賦，歎曰：「江東無我，卿當獨秀，我若無卿，亦一時之傑。

translations.literal: When he saw Zhuang's fu he sighed and said, "East of the Yangtze there would be no me—you would stand alone; without you I would still be a hero of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Reading Zhuang's fu he sighed, "East of the Yangtze, without me you would stand alone; without you I would still be a champion of the age."

sentences.zh: 」遂隱其賦。

translations.literal: He then hid his own fu.
translations.idiomatic: Then he kept his own fu hidden.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，轉司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince usurped and established himself, Zhuang was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince murdered his father and seized the throne, Zhuang was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 孝武入討，密送檄書與莊，令加改正宣佈之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu marched to suppress the usurper, he secretly sent a proclamation to Zhuang ordering him to revise and proclaim it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched to suppress the usurper, he secretly sent a proclamation draft to Zhuang with orders to revise and publish it.

sentences.zh: 莊遣腹心門生具慶奉啟事密詣孝武陳誠。

translations.literal: Zhuang sent his trusted student disciple Ju Qing with the memorial in secret to Xiaowu to declare loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang sent his trusted student Ju Qing with a secret memorial to Xiaowu pledging loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐阼，除侍中。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the throne, Zhuang was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor ascended the throne, Zhuang was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時魏求通互市，上詔群臣博議。

translations.literal: At that time Wei requested mutual markets; the Emperor ordered the ministers to debate broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wei requested border markets; the Emperor ordered a broad debate among the ministers.

sentences.zh: 莊議以為拒而觀釁，有足表強。

translations.literal: Zhuang argued that refusal while watching for provocation was sufficient to display strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang argued that refusal while watching for provocation would itself show strength.

sentences.zh: 驃騎竟陵王誕當為荊州，征丞相荊州刺史南郡王義宣入輔，義宣固辭不入，而誕便克日下船。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Prince Dan of Jingling was to go to Jing province; the Emperor summoned Chancellor and Jing Inspector Prince Yixuan of Nanjun to enter and assist, but Yixuan firmly declined; Dan at once set a day to board ship.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry General Prince Dan of Jingling was to take Jing province; the Emperor summoned Chancellor and Jing Inspector Prince Yixuan of Nanjun to enter the capital as aide, but Yixuan firmly refused, while Dan at once fixed a day to embark.

sentences.zh: 莊以丞相既無入志，而驃騎發便有期，如似欲相逼切。

translations.literal: Zhuang held that since the Chancellor had no will to enter, while the Cavalry General's departure already had a fixed day, it seemed as though one side meant to press the other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang held that since the Chancellor showed no wish to come in while the Cavalry General's departure was already dated, it looked like deliberate pressure.

sentences.zh: 帝乃申誕發日，義宣竟亦不下。

translations.literal: The Emperor then postponed Dan's departure; Yixuan in the end did not descend.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then postponed Dan's departure, and Yixuan in the end never came downriver.

sentences.zh: 于時搜才路狹，莊表陳求賢之義曰：

translations.literal: At that time the road to seek talent was narrow; Zhuang memorialized on the principle of seeking the worthy, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Talent was hard to find then; Zhuang submitted a memorial on seeking the worthy, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞功傾魏後，非特照車之珍，德柔秦客，豈徒秘璧之貴。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that merit that overturned Wei was not only the treasure that lit the carriage; virtue that softened the guest of Qin was not only the jade kept in secret.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the merit that overturned Wei was not merely the gem that lit the carriage, and the virtue that won over Qin's guest was not merely the jade kept in the vault.

sentences.zh: 隆陂所漸，成敗之由，何嘗不興資得才，替因失士。

translations.literal: What the long slope gradually moistens becomes the source of success and failure—has it not always risen with gaining talent and fallen with losing men of worth?
translations.idiomatic: What the long slope gradually waters becomes the spring of rise and fall—when has a state not flourished by winning talent and declined by losing worthy men?

sentences.zh: 故楚書以善人為寶，虞典以則哲為難。

translations.literal: Thus the Book of Chu takes good men as treasure, and the Canon of Yu finds knowing the wise difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Book of Chu calls good men treasure, and the Canon of Yu finds discerning the wise the hard part.

sentences.zh: 而進選之舉既隳中代，登造之律，未聞當今，必欲豐本康務，庇人濟俗，匪更惉懘，奚取九成。

translations.literal: Yet the promotion and selection of the middle age has already been destroyed, and the law of appointment and advancement is not heard in the present day; if one truly wishes to enrich the root and secure affairs, shelter people and aid custom, without changing the confused notes, how take the Nine Cheng?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the promotion and selection of the middle age lies in ruins, and no law of appointment is heard today; if we truly mean to strengthen the root, secure affairs, shelter people, and aid custom, without changing confused practice, how shall we reach the Nine Cheng?

sentences.zh: 夫才生於時，古今豈貳，士出於世，屯泰焉殊。

translations.literal: Talent is born of the age; how can ancient and modern differ? Scholars emerge from the world; hardship and ease are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is born of its age—how can ancient and modern be two? Men of worth arise from their times—prosperity and adversity are not alike.

sentences.zh: 升曆中陽，英賢起于徐沛，受籙白水，茂異出於荊宛。

translations.literal: When the calendar ascended at Zhongyang, heroes rose from Xu and Pei; when the tally was received at White Water, eminent men came forth from Jing and Wan.
translations.idiomatic: When the calendar rose at Zhongyang, heroes sprang from Xu and Pei; when the tally was received at White Water, eminent men came from Jing and Wan.

sentences.zh: 甯二都智之所產，七隩愚之所育，實遇與不遇、用與不用耳。

translations.literal: Were the Two Capitals only what wisdom produced, and the Seven Gorges only what folly bred? It was truly meeting or not meeting, employment or non-employment.
translations.idiomatic: Were the Two Capitals products of wisdom alone and the Seven Gorges nurseries of folly alone? It was truly a matter of being met or passed over, used or left unused.

sentences.zh: 今大道光亨，萬務俟德，而九服之曠，九流之艱，提鈞懸衡，委之選部。

translations.literal: Now the Great Way shines and all affairs await virtue, yet the emptiness of the Nine Domains and the hardship of the Nine Streams—holding the balance and hanging the steelyard—is entrusted to the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Great Way is bright and every task awaits virtue, yet the vast reaches of the Nine Domains and the straits of the Nine Streams—the balance and steelyard of selection—rest with the Selection Bureau alone.

sentences.zh: 一人之鑒易限，天下之才難源，以易限之鑒，鏡難源之才，使國罔遺賢，野無滯器，其可得乎？

translations.literal: One man's mirror is easily limited; the talent of all under heaven is hard to source; with a mirror easily limited to reflect talent hard to source—can the state leave no worthy undiscovered and the wilds hold no unused vessel?
translations.idiomatic: One man's judgment is easily bounded, yet the talent of the realm is hard to tap; to mirror boundless talent with a bounded mirror—can the state miss no worthy man and the wilds hold no unused gift?

sentences.zh: 昔公叔登臣，管仲升盜，趙文非私親疏嗣，祁奚豈諂讎比子。

translations.literal: Formerly Gongshu promoted his minister, Guan Zhong raised a robber; Zhao Wen did not favor private kin in succession, Qi Xi did not flatter an enemy's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshu once elevated his minister, Guan Zhong raised a robber; Zhao Wen did not favor a private kinsman for succession, and Qi Xi did not recommend an enemy's son from flattery.

sentences.zh: 茹茅以匯，作範前經，舉爾所知，式昭往牒。

translations.literal: Gathering mugwort for the assembly became a model in earlier classics; recommend those you know—the pattern shines in past records.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering mugwort for the assembly became a model in the classics; recommend those you know—the pattern shines in the annals.

sentences.zh: 且自古任薦，弘明賞罰，成子舉三哲而身致魏輔，應侯任二士而已捐秦相，臼季稱冀缺而疇以田采，張勃進陳湯而坐之褫爵。

translations.literal: Moreover, from antiquity appointment by recommendation made reward and punishment clear: Chengzi recommended three wise men and himself reached Wei as aide; Lord Ying employed two scholars and at once surrendered the Qin chancellorship; Jiu Ji praised Ji Que and the field fief followed; Zhang Bo advanced Chen Tang and for it was stripped of rank.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity recommendation made reward and punishment plain: Chengzi recommended three wise men and rose to aide of Wei; Lord Ying entrusted two scholars and at once gave up the Qin chancellorship; Jiu Ji praised Ji Que and received a field fief; Zhang Bo advanced Chen Tang and for it lost his rank.

sentences.zh: 此則先事之盛准，亦後王之彝鑒。

translations.literal: These are the great standards of former affairs and mirrors for later kings as well.
translations.idiomatic: These are the great precedents of earlier ages and mirrors for later rulers alike.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜普命大臣，各舉所知，以付尚書依分銓用。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that a general order should command great ministers each to recommend those they know, to be delivered to the Masters of Writing for graded appointment according to office.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that each great minister should be ordered to recommend those he knows, with the lists sent to the Masters of Writing for graded appointment.

sentences.zh: 若任得其才，舉主延賞，有不稱職，宜及其坐。

translations.literal: If the appointee proves worthy, the recommender receives extended reward; if unfit for office, the fault should reach the recommender as well.
translations.idiomatic: If the appointee proves worthy, the recommender should be rewarded; if unfit, the recommender should share the blame.

sentences.zh: 重者免黜，輕者左遷。

translations.literal: In serious cases removal and dismissal; in light cases demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Serious cases warrant dismissal; lighter ones demotion.

sentences.zh: 被舉之身，加以禁錮，年數多少，隨愆議制。

translations.literal: The recommended person should additionally be placed under restriction; the number of years should follow the fault as debated and fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The recommended man should also be barred from office for a term fixed according to the fault.

sentences.zh: 若犯大辟，則任者刑論。

translations.literal: If the crime reaches great execution, then the recommender is judged by penal law.
translations.idiomatic: If the crime reaches capital offense, the recommender faces penal judgment.

sentences.zh: 又政平訟理，莫先親人，親人之要，實歸守宰。

translations.literal: Moreover, in governing peace and settling lawsuits, nothing comes before treating kin as kin; the essence of treating kin as kin truly returns to the prefect and magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in securing peace and settling lawsuits, nothing comes before kinship rightly handled; and that essence truly rests with prefect and magistrate.

sentences.zh: 故黃霸蒞潁川累稔，杜畿居河東曆載。

translations.literal: Thus Huang Ba governed Yingchuan for many years, and Du Ji held Hedong for successive years.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ba governed Yingchuan for many years; Du Ji held Hedong year after year.

sentences.zh: 或就加恩秩，或入崇暉寵。

translations.literal: Some then received added favor in rank; some entered to receive bright favor.
translations.idiomatic: Some then received added rank and favor; some were summoned to imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 今蒞人之職，宜遵六年之限，進得章明庸惰，退得人不勤勞，如此，則上靡棄能，下無浮謬，考績之風載泰，薪槱之歌克昌。

translations.literal: Now the office of the one who governs people ought to follow a six-year limit; advancement can reveal merit and expose slackness, retirement can show whether men were diligent—thus above no talent is discarded, below no empty error floats; the wind of assessing achievement will flourish, and the song of gathering kindling will rise.
translations.idiomatic: The office of local governor should follow a six-year term: promotion would reveal merit or sloth, retirement would show who had been diligent—then above no talent is wasted, below no hollow appointment stands; the wind of assessing achievement would flourish and the song of gathering kindling rise.

sentences.zh: 初，文帝世，限年三十而仕郡縣，六周乃選代，刺史或十年餘。

translations.literal: At first, in Emperor Wen's reign, office in commanderies and counties was limited to age thirty, and after six cycles one was replaced; governors sometimes held ten years or more.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen at first, one had to reach thirty to enter commandery or county office, served six cycles before transfer, and governors sometimes held post ten years or more.

sentences.zh: 至是皆易之，仕者不拘長少，蒞人以三周為滿，宋之善政於是乎衰。

translations.literal: By now all this was changed; office holders were not bound by age, and governors served three cycles as full term—Song's good governance declined from this.
translations.idiomatic: By now all this was changed: office no longer waited on age, and governors served three cycles as a full term—Song's good governance waned from that point.

sentences.zh: 是年，拜吏部尚書，莊素多疾，不願居選部，與大司馬江夏王義恭箋，自陳「兩脅癖疢，殆與生俱，一月發動，不減兩三。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing; Zhuang by nature had many illnesses and did not wish to hold the Selection Bureau; he wrote to Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, declaring himself: "A pain in both flanks, nearly born with me—once a month it strikes, no fewer than two or three times.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing; Zhuang was often ill and did not wish to head selection; he wrote to Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, saying, "A pain in both flanks has been with me nearly from birth—it flares once a month, no fewer than two or three times.

sentences.zh: 每痛來逼心，氣餘如綖，利患數年，遂成痼疾。

translations.literal: When the pain comes it presses the heart; breath remains like a thread; the illness of sharp pain has continued several years and has become a chronic disease.
translations.idiomatic: When it comes it crushes the heart and breath hangs by a thread; this sharp pain has lasted years and become chronic.

sentences.zh: 岋岋惙惙，常如行屍。

translations.literal: Faltering and weary, always like a walking corpse.
translations.idiomatic: I falter and flag, always like a walking corpse.

sentences.zh: 眼患五月來便不復得夜坐，恒閉帷避風。

translations.literal: Eye trouble since the fifth month has kept me from sitting at night; I always close curtains to avoid wind.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fifth month my eyes will not let me sit at night; I keep the curtains drawn against the wind.

sentences.zh: 晝夜惛懵，為此不復得朝謁諸王，慶吊親舊。

translations.literal: Day and night I am muddled and dazed; for this I can no longer attend court to visit the princes or go to congratulations and mourning for kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night I am dazed and dim; for this I can no longer attend princes at court or go to congratulations and mourning for kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 今之所止，唯在小合。

translations.literal: Where I now stop is only a small side room.
translations.idiomatic: Where I now live is only a small side room.

sentences.zh: 下官微命，於天下至輕，在己不能不重。

translations.literal: The low office to which I am summoned is lightest under heaven, yet to myself it cannot but be heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The office to which I am summoned is among the lightest under heaven, yet to me it cannot but weigh heavily.

sentences.zh: 家世無年，亡高祖四十，曾祖三十三，亡祖四十七，下官新歲便三十五。

translations.literal: In my family no one has lived long: my late great-grandfather forty, my late grandfather thirty-three, my late father forty-seven; I myself this new year will be thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: No man in my line has lived long: my great-grandfather died at forty, my grandfather at thirty-three, my father at forty-seven; I myself turn thirty-five this year.

sentences.zh: 加以疾患如此，當復幾時？

translations.literal: Add illness such as this—how much longer can there be?
translations.idiomatic: Add illness such as this—how much time remains?

sentences.zh: 入年當申前請，以死自固。

translations.literal: Entering the year I should renew my former request and hold to death as firmness.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the new year I should renew my earlier plea and hold fast even unto death.

sentences.zh: 願侍坐言次，賜垂接助「。

translations.literal: I beg, when you are seated in conversation, to grant me your aid."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that when you are seated in conversation you grant me your help."

sentences.zh: 三年，坐疾多免官。

translations.literal: In the third year, because of frequent illness he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was removed from office for chronic illness.

sentences.zh: 五年，又為侍中，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary and headed the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary and headed the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 時孝武出行夜還，敕開門。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu went out and returned at night; he ordered the gate opened.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Xiaowu went out and returned at night and ordered the gate opened.

sentences.zh: 莊居守，以棨信或虛，須墨詔乃開。

translations.literal: Zhuang was holding the capital; because the tally and message might be false, he required an ink edict before opening.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was holding the capital; fearing the tally might be forged, he insisted on an ink edict before opening the gate.

sentences.zh: 上後因宴，從容曰：「卿欲效郅君章邪？

translations.literal: Later at a banquet the Emperor said with ease, "Do you wish to imitate Lord Zhi of Ye?"
translations.idiomatic: Later at a banquet the Emperor said lightly, "Do you mean to imitate Lord Zhi of Ye?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣聞搜巡有度，郊祀有節，盤于游田，著之前誡。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant has heard that patrols have their measure and suburban sacrifice has its season; dwelling at the hunting park is recorded in earlier admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have heard that patrols have their limits and suburban rites their seasons; lingering at the hunting park is warned against in earlier admonitions.

sentences.zh: 陛下今蒙犯塵露，晨往宵還，容致不逞之徒，妄生矯詐，臣是以伏須神筆。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty now braves dust and dew, going out at dawn and returning at night—perhaps unbridled men might falsely forge orders; your servant therefore waited for the imperial brush."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now braves dust and dew, leaving at dawn and returning at night—reckless men might forge an order; I therefore waited for the imperial brush."

sentences.zh: 六年，又為吏部尚書，領國子博士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again became Minister of the Masters of Writing and headed the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he again became Minister of the Masters of Writing and headed the National University.

sentences.zh: 坐選公車令張奇免官，事在顏師伯傳。

translations.literal: He was removed from office for selecting Public Carriage Commandant Zhang Qi; the matter is in the biography of Yan Shibo.
translations.idiomatic: He lost office over the selection of Public Carriage Commandant Zhang Qi; the affair is in the biography of Yan Shibo.

sentences.zh: 後除吳郡太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，以為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Zhuang was made Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, Zhuang was made Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 初，孝武寵姬殷貴妃薨，莊為誄，言：「贊軌堯門」，引漢昭帝母趙婕妤堯母門事，廢帝在東宮銜之。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Xiaowu's favored consort Lady Yin died, Zhuang composed a dirge saying, "Praised is the track of the Yao Gate," citing the matter of Zhao Lady of Emperor Zhao of Han and the Yao Mother Gate; the Deposed Emperor in the Eastern Palace bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowu's favored Lady Yin died, Zhuang wrote a dirge praising "the track of the Yao Gate," alluding to Zhao Lady, mother of Emperor Zhao of Han, and the Yao Mother Gate; the Deposed Emperor in the Eastern Palace took offense.

sentences.zh: 至是遣人詰莊曰：「卿昔作殷貴妃誄，知有東宮不？

translations.literal: At this he sent men to question Zhuang, saying, "When you wrote the dirge for Lady Yin, did you know there was an Eastern Palace?"
translations.idiomatic: Now he sent men to question Zhuang: "When you wrote Lady Yin's dirge, did you know there was an Eastern Palace?"

sentences.zh: 」將誅之。

translations.literal: He was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to have him killed.

sentences.zh: 孫奉伯說帝曰：「死是人之所同，政復一往之苦，不足為困。

translations.literal: Sun Fengbo persuaded the Emperor, saying, "Death is common to all men; even a single passage of suffering is not enough to trouble one.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fengbo persuaded the Emperor: "Death is common to all; a single turn of suffering is not enough to break a man.

sentences.zh: 莊少長富貴，且系之尚方，使知天下苦劇，然後殺之未晚。

translations.literal: Zhuang from youth to age has lived in wealth and honor; bind him in the Palace Workshop and let him know the world's bitterness—then kill him and it will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang has lived in wealth and honor from youth; bind him in the Palace Workshop and let him taste the world's bitterness—then kill him and it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言有理。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Your words have reason."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Your words make sense."

sentences.zh: 」系于左尚方。

translations.literal: He was bound in the Left Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was bound in the Left Palace Workshop.

sentences.zh: 明帝定亂得出，使為赦詔。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming settled the turmoil and released him, he had Zhuang compose the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming quelled the turmoil and freed him, he had Zhuang draft the amnesty edict.

sentences.zh: 莊夜出署門方坐，命酒酌之，已微醉，傳詔停待詔成，其文甚工。

translations.literal: Zhuang at night left the office gate and had just sat down; he ordered wine poured and was already slightly drunk; the edict arrived and he waited until the draft was finished—its wording was very skilled.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhuang left the office gate and sat down, ordered wine, and was already slightly drunk; when the edict arrived he waited until the draft was done—its wording was superb.

sentences.zh: 後為尋陽王師，加中書令、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later he became Tutor to the Prince of Xunyang, additionally Director of the Masters of Writing and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Tutor to the Prince of Xunyang, with additional posts as Director of the Masters of Writing and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋加金紫光祿大夫，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with twenty trusted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further made Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with twenty trusted attendants.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右光祿大夫，諡憲子。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Xianzi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Xianzi.

sentences.zh: 所著文章四百餘首行於世。

translations.literal: Writings and essays he composed, more than four hundred pieces, circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred pieces of his writing circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 五子：揚、朏、顥、嵷、瀹，世謂莊名子以風月景山水。

translations.literal: Five sons: Yang, Fei, Hao, Song, and Yue—the age said Zhuang named his sons after wind, moon, scenery, mountains, and water.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons—Yang, Fei, Hao, Song, and Yue—men of the age said Zhuang had named his sons for wind, moon, scenery, mountains, and water.

sentences.zh: 揚位晉平太守，女為順帝皇后，追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yang held the post of Administrator of Jinping; his daughter became Empress to Emperor Shun and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang rose to Administrator of Jinping; his daughter became Emperor Shun's empress, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 朏字敬沖，幼聰慧。

translations.literal: Fei, styled Jingchong, was clever from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Fei, courtesy name Jingchong, was clever from childhood.

sentences.zh: 莊器之，常置左右。

translations.literal: Zhuang valued him and always kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang prized him and always kept him close.

sentences.zh: 十歲能屬文。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 莊游土山，使朏命篇，攬筆便就。

translations.literal: When Zhuang visited Tushan he had Fei compose a piece; Fei took the brush and finished at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuang visited Tushan he set Fei a theme; Fei took brush and finished at once.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王景文謂莊曰：「賢子足稱神童，復為後來特達。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwen of Langye told Zhuang, "Your worthy son fully deserves the name divine youth; again he stands apart among later men."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen of Langye told Zhuang, "Your worthy son fully earns the name divine youth; among later men he stands apart."

sentences.zh: 」莊撫朏背曰：「真吾家千金。

translations.literal: Zhuang stroked Fei's back and said, "Truly a thousand gold of my house."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang stroked Fei's back and said, "Truly the thousand gold of my house."

sentences.zh: 」宋孝武帝游姑孰，敕莊攜朏從駕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Song toured Guni, he ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the imperial train.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu toured Guni, he ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 詔為洞井贊，於坐奏之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a hymn to the cave well; Fei presented it at the seat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for a hymn to the cave well; Fei presented it at the banquet.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「雖小重也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Small, yet weighty."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Small in years, yet weighty in talent."

sentences.zh: 仕宋為衛將軍袁粲長史。

translations.literal: He served Song as Chief Clerk to Guard General Yuan Can.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he served as Chief Clerk to Guard General Yuan Can.

sentences.zh: 粲性簡峻，時人方之李膺。

translations.literal: Can's nature was plain and stern; men of the time compared him to Li Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Can was plain and stern by nature; contemporaries compared him to Li Ying.

sentences.zh: 朏謁退，粲曰：「謝令不死矣。

translations.literal: When Fei withdrew after an audience, Can said, "Commander Xie is not dead after all."
translations.idiomatic: When Fei withdrew after an audience, Can said, "Commander Xie is not dead after all."

sentences.zh: 」宋明帝嘗敕朏與謝鳳子超宗從鳳莊門入。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song once ordered Fei and Xie Feng's son Chao Zong to enter with Feng through Zhuang's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song once ordered Fei and Xie Feng's son Chao Zong to enter with Feng through Zhuang's gate.

sentences.zh: 二人俱至，超宗曰：「君命不可以不往。

translations.literal: Both arrived; Chao Zong said, "The lord's command cannot be disobeyed."
translations.idiomatic: Both arrived; Chao Zong said, "The sovereign's command cannot be refused."

sentences.zh: 」乃趨而入。

translations.literal: He then hurried in.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hurried in.

sentences.zh: 朏曰：「君處臣以禮。

translations.literal: Fei said, "The lord treats his minister with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Fei said, "The lord treats his minister with ritual."

sentences.zh: 」遂退不入。

translations.literal: He then withdrew and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Then he withdrew and would not enter.

sentences.zh: 時人兩稱之，以比王尊、王陽。

translations.literal: Men of the time praised both, comparing them to Wang Zun and Wang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised both, comparing them to Wang Zun and Wang Yang.

sentences.zh: 後為臨川內史，以賄見劾，袁粲寢其事。

translations.literal: Later he was Administrator of Linchuan; he was impeached for bribery, and Yuan Can suppressed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Administrator of Linchuan; impeached for bribery, he was shielded by Yuan Can.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝為驃騎將軍輔政，選朏為長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi was Cavalry General and regent, he selected Fei as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi was Cavalry General and regent, he chose Fei as Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 高帝方圖禪代，欲以朏佐命，遷左長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao was then plotting the abdication and wished Fei to assist in establishing the mandate; he transferred him to Chief Clerk of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was plotting abdication and wanted Fei to help establish the mandate; he moved him to Chief Clerk of the Left.

sentences.zh: 每夕置酒，獨與朏論魏、晉故事，言石苞不早勸晉文，死方慟哭，方之馮異，非知機也。

translations.literal: Each evening he set out wine and alone with Fei discussed Wei and Jin stories, saying Shi Bao did not early urge Jin Wen, and only when dead did he wail—compared to Feng Yi, this was not knowing the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Each evening he set out wine and alone with Fei discussed Wei and Jin history, saying Shi Bao had not urged Jin Wen early and only wailed after death—compared with Feng Yi, that was failing to read the moment.

sentences.zh: 朏曰：「昔魏臣有勸魏武即帝位，魏武曰：'有用我者，其周文王乎。

translations.literal: Fei said, "Formerly a Wei minister urged Emperor Wu of Wei to take the imperial title; Emperor Wu said, 'If anyone is to use me, is it not as King Wen of Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: Fei said, "Once a Wei minister urged Cao Cao to take the throne; Cao Cao replied, 'If anyone is to use me, will it not be as King Wen of Zhou?

sentences.zh: '晉文世事魏氏，將必終身北面。

translations.literal: Jin Wen served the Wei house all his days and would surely face north to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi served the Wei house all his days and would surely remain a subject to the end.

sentences.zh: 假使魏早依唐、虞故事，亦當三讓彌高。

translations.literal: Even if Wei had early followed the Tang and Yu precedent, there would still have been three refusals raised ever higher."
translations.idiomatic: Even had Wei followed the Tang and Yu precedent early, there would still have been three lofty refusals."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，更引王儉為左長史，以朏為侍中，領秘書監。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased; he further brought in Wang Jian as Chief Clerk of the Left and made Fei Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was displeased; he brought in Wang Jian as Chief Clerk of the Left and made Fei Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及齊受禪，朏當日在直，百僚陪位。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, Fei was on duty that day; the hundred officials took their places.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, Fei was on duty that day and the hundred officials stood in place.

sentences.zh: 侍中當解璽，朏佯不知，曰：「有何公事？

translations.literal: The Attendant-in-Ordinary should unseal the imperial seal; Fei feigned ignorance and said, "What public business is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant-in-Ordinary was to unseal the imperial seal; Fei feigned ignorance and said, "What public business is there?"

sentences.zh: 」傳詔雲，「解璽授齊王」。

translations.literal: The transmitted edict said, "Unseal the seal and transfer it to the King of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted edict said, "Unseal the seal and transfer it to the King of Qi."

sentences.zh: 朏曰：「齊自應有侍中。

translations.literal: Fei said, "Qi should have its own Attendant-in-Ordinary."
translations.idiomatic: Fei said, "Qi should have its own Attendant-in-Ordinary."

sentences.zh: 」乃引枕臥。

translations.literal: He then pulled up a pillow and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: Then he pulled up a pillow and lay down.

sentences.zh: 傳詔懼，乃使稱疾，欲取兼人。

translations.literal: The messenger was afraid and then had him reported ill, wishing to fetch a substitute.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger panicked and had him reported ill, intending to fetch a substitute.

sentences.zh: 朏曰：「我無疾，何所道。

translations.literal: Fei said, "I have no illness—what is there to report?"
translations.idiomatic: Fei said, "I am not ill—what is there to report?"

sentences.zh: 」遂朝服出東掖門，乃得車，仍還宅。

translations.literal: He then went out the East Side Gate in court dress, got a carriage, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went out the East Side Gate in court dress, found a carriage, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 是日，遂以王儉為侍中解璽。

translations.literal: That day Wang Jian was made Attendant-in-Ordinary to unseal the seal.
translations.idiomatic: That day Wang Jian was made Attendant-in-Ordinary to unseal the seal.

sentences.zh: 既而武帝請誅朏，高帝曰：「殺之則成其名，正應容之度外。

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Wu asked to execute Fei; Emperor Gao said, "To kill him would make his name; one should simply leave him outside the measure."
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wu asked to execute Fei; Gao said, "Killing him would make his fame; better leave him outside the pale."

sentences.zh: 」又以家貧乞郡，辭旨抑揚，詔免官禁錮五年。

translations.literal: Again, because his family was poor he begged a commandery; his memorial's tone was restrained and elevated; an edict removed him from office and placed him under restriction for five years.
translations.idiomatic: Again, pleading poverty he begged a commandery post; his memorial was measured yet proud; an edict stripped him of office and barred him for five years.

sentences.zh: 永明中，為義興太守，在郡不省雜事，悉付綱紀，曰：「吾不能作主者吏，但能作太守耳。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he was Administrator of Yixing; in the commandery he did not attend to miscellaneous affairs but entrusted all to the clerks, saying, "I cannot be the clerk who does the work—I can only be the Administrator."
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming era he was Administrator of Yixing; in the commandery he ignored routine business and left everything to the clerks, saying, "I cannot be the clerk who runs affairs—I can only be the Administrator."

sentences.zh: 」曆都官尚書，中書令，侍中，領新安王師。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Minister of Revenue, Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Tutor to Prince Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Minister of Revenue, Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Tutor to Prince Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 求出，仍為吳興太守。

translations.literal: He requested to leave and again became Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave office and again became Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 明帝謀入嗣位，引朝廷舊臣，朏內圖止足，且實避事。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming plotted to enter and succeed; he drew in old ministers of the court; Fei inwardly meant to know when to stop and in truth wished to avoid affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming plotted succession he summoned old court ministers; Fei inwardly sought sufficiency and truly wished to avoid public business.

sentences.zh: 弟瀹時為吏部尚書，朏至郡，致瀹數斛酒，遺書曰：「可力飲此，勿豫人事。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yue was then Minister of the Masters of Writing; when Fei reached the commandery he sent Yue several hu of wine with a letter saying, "Drink this with force; do not meddle in human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yue was then Minister of the Masters of Writing; reaching the commandery Fei sent Yue several hu of wine with a note: "Drink hard and stay out of affairs."

sentences.zh: 」朏居郡，每不理，常務聚斂，眾頗譏之，亦不屑也。

translations.literal: Fei in the commandery often neglected governance and constantly pursued accumulation; many mocked him, yet he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery Fei often neglected governance and constantly pursued gain; many mocked him, yet he cared nothing.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，徵為侍中、中書令，不應。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu four he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing; he refused.

sentences.zh: 遣諸子還都，獨與母留，築室郡之西郭。

translations.literal: He sent his sons back to the capital and remained alone with his mother, building a house in the west suburb of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his sons back to the capital and stayed alone with his mother, building a house in the commandery's western suburb.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔加優禮，旌其素概，賜床帳褥席，奉以卿祿。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's edict added special honors, commending his plain integrity, and granted bed curtains, mats, and stipend of a full minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming added special honors, praising his plain integrity, and granted bedding and a minister's stipend.

sentences.zh: 時國子祭酒廬江何胤亦抗表還會稽。

translations.literal: At that time National University Chancellor He Yin of Lujiang also submitted a memorial to return to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Then National University Chancellor He Yin of Lujiang also memorialized to return to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 永元中，詔征朏、胤，並不屈。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era an edict summoned Fei and Yin; both refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongyuan era edicts summoned Fei and Yin; both refused.

sentences.zh: 時東昏皆命迫遣，會梁武帝起兵。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Donghun ordered forced dispatch; then Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Donghun ordered forced summons; soon Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops.

sentences.zh: 及建鄴平，征朏、胤，並補軍諮祭酒，皆不至。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Fei and Yin were summoned and appointed Army Advisers and Sacrificial Officers; neither came.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang was pacified, Fei and Yin were summoned as Army Advisers and Sacrificial Officers; neither came.

sentences.zh: 及即位，詔征朏為侍中、左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，胤散騎常侍、特進、右光祿大夫，又並不屈。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, an edict summoned Fei as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Left of the Purple Ribbon, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Yin as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Special Advance, and Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon; again both refused.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession edicts summoned Fei as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Left of the Purple Ribbon, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Yin as Regular Attendant, Special Advance, and Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon; again both refused.

sentences.zh: 仍遣領軍司馬王果敦譬朏，朏謀于何胤，胤欲獨高其節，紿曰：「興王之世，安可久處？」

translations.literal: He then sent General of the Guards Sima Wang Guo to urge Fei; Fei consulted He Yin; Yin wished alone to elevate his integrity and deceived him, saying, "In an age of rising kings, how can one long remain apart?"
translations.idiomatic: Then General of the Guards Sima Wang Guo was sent to persuade Fei; Fei consulted He Yin; Yin, wishing to stand alone in integrity, deceived him: "In an age of rising kings, how can one stay apart forever?"

sentences.zh: 明年六月，朏輕舟出，詣闕自陳。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year Fei went out in a light boat and came to the palace to declare himself.
translations.idiomatic: The next sixth month Fei went out in a light boat and came to court to declare himself.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「子陵遂能屈志。

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said, "Ziling can indeed bend his will."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled and said, "Ziling can indeed bend his will after all."

sentences.zh: 」詔以為侍中、司徒、尚書令。

translations.literal: An edict made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 朏辭腳疾，不堪拜謁，乃角巾肩輿詣雲龍門謝。

translations.literal: Fei pleaded foot illness and could not perform bowing audiences; he therefore went in kerchief and shoulder carriage to thank at the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fei pleaded foot ailment and could not perform bowing audiences; he came in kerchief and shoulder carriage to give thanks at the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 詔見於華林園，乘小車就席。

translations.literal: An edict received him in the Hualin Garden; he came in a small carriage to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict received him in Hualin Garden; he came in a small carriage to his seat.

sentences.zh: 明旦，乘輿出幸朏宅，宴語盡歡。

translations.literal: The next morning the imperial carriage went out to visit Fei's house; they feasted and talked to full delight.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning the imperial carriage visited Fei's house; they feasted and talked with full delight.

sentences.zh: 朏固陳本志，不許。

translations.literal: Fei firmly stated his original intent; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fei firmly stated his original intent; the Emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 又固請自還迎母，許之。

translations.literal: Again he firmly requested to return and meet his mother; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Again he firmly asked to return and fetch his mother; this was granted.

sentences.zh: 臨發，輿駕臨幸，賦詩餞別，王人送迎相望於道。

translations.literal: At departure the imperial carriage came to send him off; poems were composed to bid farewell; imperial envoys lined the road seeing him off.
translations.idiomatic: At departure the Emperor came to send him off with poems of farewell; imperial envoys lined the road.

sentences.zh: 到都，敕材官起府於舊宅。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, an edict ordered craftsmen to build a mansion at his old residence.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the capital, an edict ordered craftsmen to build a mansion at his old residence.

sentences.zh: 武帝臨軒，遣謁者於府拜授。

translations.literal: The Emperor came to the hall; he sent a Herald to the mansion to confer appointment by bow.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came to the hall and sent a Herald to the mansion to confer appointment by bow.

sentences.zh: 詔停諸公事及朔望朝謁。

translations.literal: An edict stopped all public business and new-moon and full-moon court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exempted him from public business and from new-moon and full-moon audiences.

sentences.zh: 三年元會，詔朏乘小輿升殿。

translations.literal: At the third year's New Year assembly, an edict ordered Fei to ascend the hall in a small carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At the third year's New Year assembly an edict ordered Fei to ascend the hall in a small carriage.

sentences.zh: 朏素憚煩，及居台鉉，兼掌內台，職事多不覽，以此頗失眾望。

translations.literal: Fei by nature feared trouble; once he held the high offices and additionally managed the inner secretariat, he often did not review duties; for this he lost much popular hope.
translations.idiomatic: Fei by nature shunned bother; holding high office and additionally managing the inner secretariat, he often skipped business, and for this lost much public esteem.

sentences.zh: 其年母憂，尋有詔攝職如故。

translations.literal: That year his mother died; soon an edict ordered him to resume duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: That year his mother died; soon an edict ordered him to resume duties as before.

sentences.zh: 建武初，朏為吳興，以雞卵賦人，收雞數千。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, when Fei was in Wuxing, he levied an egg tax on the people and collected several thousand chickens.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu, while Fei was in Wuxing, he levied an egg tax and collected several thousand chickens.

sentences.zh: 及遯節不全，為清談所少。

translations.literal: And his integrity was not complete; pure talkers held him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity was also incomplete; men of pure talk thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 著書及文章行於世。

translations.literal: Books and essays he wrote circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His books and essays circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 子諼，位司徒右長史，坐殺牛廢黜。
