translations.literal: His son Xuan held the post of Chief Clerk of the Right of the Minister of Works and was dismissed for slaughtering an ox.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan rose to Chief Clerk of the Right of the Minister of Works and was dismissed for slaughtering an ox.

sentences.zh: 為東陽內史，及還，五官送錢一萬，止留一百。

translations.literal: As Administrator of Dongyang, on returning the Five Offices sent ten thousand coins; he kept only one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: As Administrator of Dongyang, on returning the Five Offices sent ten thousand coins; he kept only one hundred.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「數多劉寵，更以為愧。」

translations.literal: He replied, "The number exceeds Liu Chong—this makes me all the more ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The sum exceeds Liu Chong—I am all the more ashamed."

sentences.zh: 次子譓，不妄交接，門無雜賓。

translations.literal: The second son Hui did not associate lightly; no mixed guests at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Hui kept no casual company; no mixed guests crossed his gate.

sentences.zh: 有時獨醉，曰：「入吾室者但有清風，對吾飲者唯當明月。

translations.literal: Sometimes he drank alone and said, "Those who enter my room find only clear wind; those who drink with me should have only the bright moon."
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he drank alone and said, "Those who enter my room meet only clear wind; those who drink with me should have only the bright moon."

sentences.zh: 」位右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He held the post of Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 子哲，字穎豫，美風儀，舉止醞藉，襟情豁朗，為士君子所重。

translations.literal: His son Zhe, styled Yingyu, had fine bearing; his conduct was refined and open; men and gentlemen esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhe, courtesy name Yingyu, had fine bearing and refined, open manner; gentlemen esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 仕梁至廣陵太守，侯景之亂，因寓居焉。

translations.literal: He served Liang to Administrator of Guangling; during Hou Jing's rebellion he lodged there.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he rose to Administrator of Guangling and lodged there during Hou Jing's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 仕陳曆吏部尚書，中書令，侍中，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Under Chen he successively held Minister of the Masters of Writing, Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chen he held Minister of the Masters of Writing, Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡康子。

translations.literal: When he died his posthumous title was Kangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his posthumous title was Kangzi.

sentences.zh: 顥字仁悠，朏弟也。

translations.literal: Hao, styled Renyou, was Fei's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, courtesy name Renyou, was Fei's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少簡靜。

translations.literal: From youth he was plain and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was plain and quiet.

sentences.zh: 宋末為豫章太守，至石頭，遂白服登烽火樓，坐免官。

translations.literal: At the end of Song he was Administrator of Yuzhang; reaching Shitou he then went in white dress to ascend the beacon tower and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Song he was Administrator of Yuzhang; reaching Shitou he climbed the beacon tower in white dress and was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 詣齊高帝自占謝，言辭清麗，容儀端雅，左右為之傾目，宥而不問。

translations.literal: He went to Emperor Gao of Qi to explain himself; his words were clear and beautiful, his bearing upright and elegant; those beside him turned their eyes; he was pardoned and not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Gao to explain himself; his speech was clear and elegant, his bearing upright; those beside him stared; he was pardoned without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 齊永明初，高選友學，以顥為竟陵王友。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming in Qi, in high selection of companion scholars, Hao was made Companion to Prince Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming, in the high selection of companion scholars, Hao was made Companion to Prince Jingling.

sentences.zh: 曆吏部郎，有簡秀之目。

translations.literal: He successively held Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and had the reputation of plain elegance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and was known for plain elegance.

sentences.zh: 卒于北中郎長史。

translations.literal: He died as Chief Clerk to the General of the North.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Chief Clerk to the General of the North.

sentences.zh: 顥弟瀹字義潔。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Yue, styled Yijie.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Yue, courtesy name Yijie.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，王景文見而異之，言于宋孝武，召見於人眾中。

translations.literal: At seven, Wang Jingwen saw him and was struck; he spoke to Emperor Xiaowu of Song; the Emperor summoned him among the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: At seven Wang Jingwen saw him and marveled; he spoke to Emperor Xiaowu, who summoned him before the crowd.

sentences.zh: 瀹舉止閑詳，應對合旨，帝悅，詔尚公主，景和敗，事寢。

translations.literal: Yue's bearing was leisurely and detailed; his replies fit the intent; the Emperor was pleased and ordered him to marry the princess; when Jinghe fell the matter was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's bearing was calm and precise, his answers apt; the Emperor was pleased and ordered a princess for him; when Jinghe fell the match was suspended.

sentences.zh: 僕射褚彥回以女妻之，厚為資送。

translations.literal: Vice Director Chu Yanhui gave him his daughter in marriage with a rich dowry.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Chu Yanhui gave him his daughter with a rich dowry.

sentences.zh: 性甚敏贍，嘗與劉悛飲，推讓久之，悛曰：「謝莊兒不可雲不能飲。

translations.literal: His nature was very quick and resourceful; once drinking with Liu Jiao, after long deferral Jiao said, "Xie Zhuang's son cannot be said unable to drink."
translations.idiomatic: He was quick and resourceful; once drinking with Liu Jiao, after long deferral Jiao said, "Xie Zhuang's son cannot be called unable to drink."

sentences.zh: 」瀹曰：「苟得其人，自可流湎千日。

translations.literal: Yue said, "If one finds the right man, one can indeed drink a thousand days deep."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "With the right company one could indeed drink deep for a thousand days."

sentences.zh: 」悛甚慚，無言。

translations.literal: Jiao was greatly ashamed and had no words.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was deeply ashamed and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 仕齊累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Qi he successively rose to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he rose to Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 衛軍王儉引為長史，雅相禮遇。

translations.literal: Guard General Wang Jian brought him in as Chief Clerk and treated him with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Guard General Wang Jian took him as Chief Clerk and honored him with ritual courtesy.

sentences.zh: 後拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 明帝廢郁林，領兵入殿，左右驚走報瀹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming deposed Prince of Yulin and led troops into the hall, attendants ran in alarm to report to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming deposed Prince of Yulin and led troops into the hall, attendants ran in alarm to Yue.

sentences.zh: 瀹與客圍棋，每下子，輒云：「其當有意」，竟局乃還齋臥，竟不問外事。

translations.literal: Yue was playing weiqi with a guest; with each move he would say, "That must have intent"; when the game ended he returned to his room and slept, never asking about outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was playing weiqi with a guest; with each stone he said, "That must mean something"; when the game ended he returned to his room and slept, never asking about outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，瀹又屬疾，不知公事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Yue again claimed illness and knew nothing of public business.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Yue again claimed illness and ignored public business.

sentences.zh: 蕭諶以兵臨起之，瀹曰：「天下事，公卿處之足矣；

translations.literal: Xiao Chen came with troops to rouse him; Yue said, "Affairs under heaven—let the lords and ministers settle them;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen came with troops to rouse him; Yue said, "Affairs under heaven—let the lords and ministers handle them;

sentences.zh: 且死者命也，何足以此懼人。」

translations.literal: besides, death is fate—what need to frighten people with it?"
translations.idiomatic: besides, death is fate—why frighten people with it?"

sentences.zh: 後宴會功臣上酒，尚書令王晏等興席，瀹獨不起，曰：「陛下受命應天，王晏以為己力。

translations.literal: Later at a banquet rewarding meritorious ministers with wine, Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan and others rose from their seats; Yue alone did not rise and said, "Your Majesty received the Mandate in accord with Heaven—Wang Yan thinks it his own doing."
translations.idiomatic: Later at a banquet honoring meritorious ministers with wine, Director Wang Yan and others rose; Yue alone stayed seated and said, "Your Majesty received the Mandate in accord with Heaven—Wang Yan thinks it his own work."

sentences.zh: 」獻觴遂不見報。

translations.literal: He offered the cup and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He offered the cup and received no reply.

sentences.zh: 上大笑解之。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly and smoothed it over.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and smoothed it over.

sentences.zh: 座罷，晏呼瀹共載，欲相撫悅，瀹又正色曰：「君巢窟在何處？

translations.literal: When the seats ended Yan called Yue to share a carriage, wishing to win him over; Yue again said with stern face, "Where is your nest and burrow?"
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended Yan called Yue to share a carriage, hoping to win him; Yue again said sternly, "Where is your nest and burrow?"

sentences.zh: 」晏初得班劍，瀹謂曰：「身家太傅，裁得六人，若何事頓得二十？

translations.literal: When Yan first received the gilded sword, Yue told him, "Your family produced a Grand Tutor and got only six men—why suddenly twenty for one affair?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan first received the gilded sword, Yue told him, "Your house produced a Grand Tutor and got only six guards—why suddenly twenty for one affair?"

sentences.zh: 」晏甚憚之，謂江祏曰：「彼上人者，難為酬對。

translations.literal: Yan greatly feared him and told Jiang Shi, "That lofty man—hard to match in reply."
translations.idiomatic: Yan greatly feared him and told Jiang Shi, "That lofty man is hard to answer."

sentences.zh: 」加領右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 兄朏在吳興，論啟公事稽晚，瀹輒代朏為啟，上知非朏手跡，被問見原。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Fei was in Wuxing, memorials on public business were often late; Yue would draft them for Fei; the Emperor knew it was not Fei's hand and questioned him, but pardoned him when he saw the truth.
translations.idiomatic: When Fei was in Wuxing, memorials on public business were often late; Yue drafted them for him; the Emperor knew the hand was not Fei's and questioned him, but pardoned him on learning the truth.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，卒于太子詹事，贈金紫光祿大夫，諡簡子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he died as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai one he died as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 初，朏為吳興，瀹於征虜渚送別，朏指瀹口曰：「此中唯宜飲酒。

translations.literal: At first, when Fei was in Wuxing, Yue saw him off at Zhengliu Isle; Fei pointed at Yue's mouth and said, "Here one should only drink wine."
translations.idiomatic: When Fei was in Wuxing, Yue saw him off at Zhengliu Isle; Fei pointed at Yue's mouth and said, "Here one should only drink wine."

sentences.zh: 」瀹建武之朝，專以長酣為事，與劉瑱、沈昭略交，飲各至數斗。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu court Yue devoted himself to long drinking; he associated with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolue, each drinking several dou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu court Yue devoted himself to long drinking; with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolue he each drank several dou.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝問王儉：「當今誰能為五言？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi asked Wang Jian, "Who today can write five-character verse?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi asked Wang Jian, "Who today can write five-character verse?"

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「朏得父膏腴，江淹有意。

translations.literal: Jian said, "Fei got his father's richness; Jiang Yan has the intent."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Fei inherited his father's richness; Jiang Yan has the intent."

sentences.zh: 」上起禪靈寺，敕瀹撰碑文。

translations.literal: The Emperor raised the Chanling Temple and ordered Yue to compose the stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor built Chanling Temple and ordered Yue to compose the stele inscription.

sentences.zh: 瀹子覽。

translations.literal: Yue's son Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son was Lan.

sentences.zh: 覽字景滌，選尚齊錢唐公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Lan, styled Jingdi, was selected to marry the Princess of Qiantang of Qi and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Lan, courtesy name Jingdi, was chosen to marry the Princess of Qiantang of Qi and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 梁武平建鄴，朝士王亮、王瑩等數人揖，自餘皆拜，覽時年二十餘，為太子舍人，亦長揖而已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang, court gentlemen Wang Liang, Wang Ying, and several others bowed with a clasped-hand salute; the rest all bowed; Lan was then just over twenty, Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and also gave only the clasped-hand salute.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang pacified Jiankang, court gentlemen Wang Liang, Wang Ying, and several others gave the clasped-hand salute while the rest bowed; Lan, just over twenty and Attendant to the Heir Apparent, also gave only the clasped-hand salute.

sentences.zh: 意氣閒雅，視瞻聰明，武帝目送良久，謂徐勉曰：「覺此生芳蘭竟體，想謝莊政當如此。

translations.literal: His spirit was easy and elegant, his gaze bright; the Emperor watched him a long time as he departed and told Xu Mian, "I feel this man's body is fragrant orchid throughout—I think Xie Zhuang must have been like this."
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was easy and elegant, his gaze bright; the Emperor watched him long as he left and told Xu Mian, "This man's body seems all fragrant orchid—I think Xie Zhuang must have been like this."

sentences.zh: 」自此仍被賞味。

translations.literal: From this he continued to be prized.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he continued to be prized.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，為中書侍郎，掌吏部事，頃之即真。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was Gentleman of the Secretariat, managing the Masters of Writing; soon he received full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian one he was Gentleman of the Secretariat, managing the Masters of Writing; soon he received full appointment.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍坐，受敕與侍中王暕為詩答贈，其文甚工，乃使重作，復合旨。

translations.literal: Once attending seated, he received an order with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Xie to compose answering poems; the wording was very skilled, and he was made to rewrite it; again it fit the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Once while attending he was ordered with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Xie to compose answering poems; the wording was superb, and when told to rewrite it he again hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 帝賜詩云：「雙文既後進，二少實名家，豈伊爾棟隆，信乃俱國華。

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed a poem saying, "Shuangwen is the later arrival; the two young men are truly great houses—is it not you who raise the beam, truly both flowers of the state?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor bestowed a poem: "Shuangwen comes after, yet the two young men are truly great houses—is it not you who raise the beam, both flowers of the state?"

sentences.zh: 」為侍中，頗樂酒，因宴席與散騎常侍蕭琛辭相詆毀，為有司所奏。

translations.literal: As Attendant-in-Ordinary he greatly enjoyed wine; at a banquet he exchanged insults with Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Xiao Chen and was reported by the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: As Attendant-in-Ordinary he greatly enjoyed wine; at a banquet he traded insults with Regular Attendant Xiao Chen and was reported by the relevant office.

sentences.zh: 武帝以覽年少不直，出為中權長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Lan was young and not upright, sent him out as Chief Clerk to the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, judging Lan young and not upright, sent him out as Chief Clerk to the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 後拜吏部尚書，出為吳興太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing and sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing and sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人黃睦之家居烏程，子弟專橫，前太守皆折節事之。

translations.literal: Palace Aide Huang Muzhi's family lived in Wucheng; his sons and younger brothers were domineering; previous administrators all bent ritual to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Aide Huang Muzhi's family lived in Wucheng; his sons and brothers were domineering; previous administrators all bowed to them.

sentences.zh: 覽未到郡，睦之子弟迎覽，覽逐去其船，杖吏為通者，自是睦之家杜門不出。

translations.literal: Before Lan reached the commandery, Muzhi's sons and younger brothers came to meet Lan; Lan drove off their boat and beat the clerk who had passed messages; from then Muzhi's family closed their gate and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lan reached the commandery, Muzhi's sons came to meet him; Lan drove off their boat and beat the clerk who had carried messages; from then Muzhi's family shut their gate.

sentences.zh: 郡境多劫，為東道患，覽下車肅然。

translations.literal: Within the commandery were many bandits, a scourge on the eastern road; when Lan took office order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had many bandits, a scourge on the eastern road; when Lan took office order returned.

sentences.zh: 初齊明帝及覽父瀹、東海徐孝嗣並為吳興，號為名守，覽皆過之。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Ming of Qi and Lan's father Yue and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all been Administrators of Wuxing and were called famous governors; Lan surpassed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi, Lan's father Yue, and Xu Xiaosi of Donghai had all governed Wuxing as famed administrators; Lan surpassed them all.

sentences.zh: 覽昔在新安，頗聚斂，至是遂稱廉潔，時人方之王述。

translations.literal: Lan formerly in Xin'an had greatly accumulated wealth; by now he was called incorrupt; men of the time compared him to Wang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lan had greatly accumulated wealth in Xin'an; now he was called incorrupt; contemporaries compared him to Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，贈中書令。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 覽弟舉字言揚，幼好學，與覽齊名。

translations.literal: Lan's younger brother Ju, styled Yanyang, loved learning from youth and was as famed as Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's younger brother Ju, courtesy name Yanyang, loved learning from youth and was as famed as Lan.

sentences.zh: 年十四，嘗贈沈約詩，為約所賞。

translations.literal: At fourteen he once sent a poem to Shen Yue and was praised by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he once sent Shen Yue a poem and won Yue's praise.

sentences.zh: 弱冠丁父憂，幾致毀滅。

translations.literal: At twenty he entered mourning for his father and nearly destroyed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered mourning for his father and nearly wasted away.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為太常博士，與兄覽俱預元會。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was Doctor of the Grand Master of Ceremonies and with his elder brother Lan both attended the New Year assembly.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was Doctor of the Grand Master of Ceremonies and with his elder brother Lan attended the New Year assembly.

sentences.zh: 江淹一見並相欽挹，曰：「所謂'馭二龍于長塗'者也。」

translations.literal: Jiang Yan saw them both and admired them together, saying, "This is what is meant by 'driving two dragons on the long road.'"
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan saw them both and admired them, saying, "This is 'driving two dragons on the long road.'"

sentences.zh: 為太子家令，掌管記，深為詔明太子賞接。

translations.literal: He was Household Steward to the Heir Apparent and headed the secretariat; he was deeply favored and received by Crown Prince Zhaoming.
translations.idiomatic: He was Household Steward to the Heir Apparent and headed the secretariat; Crown Prince Zhaoming deeply favored and received him.

sentences.zh: 秘書監任昉出為新安郡，別舉詩云：「詎念耋嗟人，方深老夫托。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Ren Fang went out as Administrator of Xin'an; in parting Ju composed a poem saying, "How can one remember the sighing old man—yet you deeply trust this old man's charge."
translations.idiomatic: Director Ren Fang went out as Administrator of Xin'an; Ju wrote in parting, "How can one remember the sighing elder—yet you deeply trust this old man's charge."

sentences.zh: 」其屬意如此。

translations.literal: His intent was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his intent.

sentences.zh: 梁武嘗訪舉於覽，覽曰：「識藝過臣甚遠，唯飲酒不及於臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Ju through Lan; Lan said, "His learning and talent far exceed mine; only in drinking he does not match me."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked about Ju through Lan; Lan said, "His learning and talent far exceed mine; only in drinking he falls short of me."

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尋除安成郡守，母往於郡喪，辭不赴。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Ancheng; his mother died in the commandery and he declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Administrator of Ancheng; his mother died in the commandery and he declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 歷位左戶尚書，遷掌吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He successively held Minister of the Left Household and was transferred to head the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of the Left Household and was transferred to head the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 舉祖莊、父瀹、兄覽並經此職，前代少比。

translations.literal: Ju's grandfather Zhuang, father Yue, and elder brother Lan had all held this office; few in former ages could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's grandfather Zhuang, father Yue, and elder brother Lan had all held this office—few in former ages could compare.

sentences.zh: 舉尤長玄理及釋氏義，為晉陵郡時，常與義學僧遞講經論，征士何胤自虎丘山出赴之，其盛如此。

translations.literal: Ju was especially skilled in dark learning and Buddhist meaning; when he was Administrator of Jinling he often debated scripture and treatises in turn with monks of the faith, and recluse He Yin came from Tiger Hill to attend—the splendor was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was especially skilled in dark learning and Buddhist doctrine; as Administrator of Jinling he often debated scripture with monks of the faith, and recluse He Yin came from Tiger Hill to attend—such was the splendor.

sentences.zh: 先是，北度人盧廣有儒術，為國子博士，于學發講，僕射徐勉以下畢至。

translations.literal: Before this, Lu Guang of the northern crossing had Confucian learning and was Doctor of the National University; in the academy he opened lectures and Vice Director Xu Mian and those below all came.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lu Guang of the northern crossing had Confucian learning and was Doctor of the National University; he opened lectures in the academy and Vice Director Xu Mian and all below came.

sentences.zh: 舉造坐屢折廣，辭理遒邁。

translations.literal: Ju took his seat and repeatedly refuted Guang; his reasoning was forceful and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Ju took his seat and repeatedly refuted Guang; his reasoning was forceful and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 廣深嘆服，仍以所執麈尾、斑竹杖、滑石書格薦之，以況重席焉。

translations.literal: Guang sighed deeply in submission and moreover presented the fly-whisk, spotted bamboo staff, and smooth-stone writing frame he held, comparing him to the honored mat.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sighed and submitted, then presented the fly-whisk, spotted bamboo staff, and smooth-stone writing frame he held, honoring him as one would a master on the mat.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to Vice Director of the Right Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to Vice Director of the Right Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 大同三年，出為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he went out as Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong three he went out as Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 先是，何敬容居郡有美績，世稱為「何吳郡」。

translations.literal: Before this, He Jingrong in governing the commandery had fine achievements; the world called him "He of Wu Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Before this He Jingrong had governed the commandery with fine achievement; the world called him "He of Wu Commandery."

sentences.zh: 及舉為政，聲跡略相比。

translations.literal: When Ju governed, reputation and traces were roughly comparable.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju governed, reputation and record were roughly comparable.

sentences.zh: 曾要何征君講中論，何難以巾褐入南門，乃從東園進。

translations.literal: Once he invited Recluse He to lecture on the Middle Treatise; He found it hard to enter the south gate in cloth cap and robe and therefore came through the east garden.
translations.idiomatic: Once he invited Recluse He to lecture on the Middle Treatises; He found it hard to enter the south gate in scholar's dress and came through the east garden.

sentences.zh: 致詩往復，為虎丘山賦題於寺。

translations.literal: They exchanged poems back and forth and set the theme of a fu on Tiger Hill at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged poems and set the theme of a fu on Tiger Hill at the temple.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、太子詹事、翊左將軍。

translations.literal: He entered as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, and General Who Assists the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, and General Who Assists the Left.

sentences.zh: 舉父瀹齊時終此官，累表乞改，敕不許。

translations.literal: Ju's father Yue under Qi ended in this office; Ju repeatedly memorialized begging to change it; the edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's father Yue under Qi had died in this office; Ju repeatedly begged to change it; the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 後遷尚書僕射，侍中、將軍如故。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Attendant-in-Ordinary and General as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Attendant-in-Ordinary and General unchanged.

sentences.zh: 舉雖屢居端揆，未嘗肯預時政，保身固寵，不能有所發明。

translations.literal: Though Ju repeatedly held the highest offices, he never would intervene in affairs of the time; preserving himself and securing favor, he could not bring forth illumination.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ju repeatedly held the highest offices, he never intervened in affairs of the time; preserving himself and securing favor, he brought forth no illumination.

sentences.zh: 因疾陳解，敕輒賜假，並敕處方，加給上藥，其恩遇如此。

translations.literal: Because of illness he submitted resignation; edicts repeatedly granted leave and additionally ordered prescriptions and bestowed superior medicines—the grace was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he submitted resignation; edicts repeatedly granted leave, ordered prescriptions, and bestowed superior medicines—such was the grace shown him.

sentences.zh: 侯景來降，帝詢訪朝臣，舉及朝士皆請拒之。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing came to surrender, the Emperor consulted the court ministers; Ju and the court gentlemen all asked to reject him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing came to surrender, the Emperor consulted the ministers; Ju and the court gentlemen all asked to reject him.

sentences.zh: 帝從朱異言納之，以為景能立功趙、魏。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed Zhu Yi's words and accepted him, thinking Jing could establish merit in Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed Zhu Yi's counsel and accepted him, thinking Jing could win merit in Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 舉等不敢復言。

translations.literal: Ju and the others did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Ju and the others did not dare speak again.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，遷尚書令，卒于內台。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and died in the inner secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing two he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing and died in the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「舉非止曆官已多，亦人倫儀錶，久著公望，悵恨未授之，可贈侍中、中衛將軍、開府儀同三司。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Ju not only held many offices—he was also a model of human relations, long famed in public expectation; I regret not having conferred more on him; he may be posthumously enfeoffed as Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Guard, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Ju not only held many offices—he was also a model of human conduct, long famed in public expectation; I regret not having conferred more; posthumously enfeoff him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Guard, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 舉宅內山齋舍以為寺，泉石之美，殆若自然。

translations.literal: Ju's house had a mountain study and lodge made into a temple; the beauty of spring and stone was nearly natural.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's house had a mountain study and lodge made into a temple; its springs and stones were nearly natural in beauty.

sentences.zh: 臨川、始興諸王常所遊踐。

translations.literal: Princes of Linchuan and Shixing often came to roam there.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of Linchuan and Shixing often came to roam there.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸于婁湖立園，廣燕，酒後好聚眾賓冠，手自裂破，投之唾壺，皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: Prince Lun of Shaoling set up a garden at Lou Lake with broad banquets; after wine he liked to gather the guests' caps and personally tear them and throw them into the spittoon; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lun of Shaoling built a garden at Lou Lake with broad banquets; drunk he liked to gather guests' caps, tear them himself, and throw them into the spittoon; none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 舉嘗預宴，王欲取舉幘。

translations.literal: Ju once attended a banquet; the Prince wished to take Ju's headcloth.
translations.idiomatic: Ju once attended a banquet; the Prince wished to seize Ju's headcloth.

sentences.zh: 舉正色曰：「裂冠毀冕，下官弗敢聞命。

translations.literal: Ju said with stern face, "To tear caps and ruin crowns—your servant dare not hear the command."
translations.idiomatic: Ju said sternly, "To tear caps and ruin crowns—your servant dare not hear the command."

sentences.zh: 」拂衣而退。

translations.literal: He brushed his robes and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed his robes and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王屢召不返，甚有慚色。

translations.literal: The Prince repeatedly summoned him but he did not return; he was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince repeatedly summoned him but he did not return; the Prince was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 舉托情玄勝，尤長佛理，注淨名經，常自講說。

translations.literal: Ju entrusted his feelings to dark transcendence and was especially skilled in Buddhist principle; he annotated the Vimalakirti Sutra and often lectured on it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ju entrusted his feelings to dark transcendence and was especially skilled in Buddhist principle; he annotated the Vimalakirti Sutra and often lectured on it himself.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子嘏。

translations.literal: His son was Jia.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jia.

sentences.zh: 嘏字含茂，風神清雅，頗善屬文。

translations.literal: Jia, styled Hanmao, had a spirit that was clear and elegant and was quite skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, courtesy name Hanmao, had a clear elegant spirit and was skilled at prose.

sentences.zh: 仕梁為太子中庶子，建安太守。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，之廣州依蕭勃。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he went to Guangzhou and relied on Xiao Bo.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he went to Guangzhou and relied on Xiao Bo.

sentences.zh: 勃敗，在周迪門。

translations.literal: When Bo was defeated he was in Zhou Di's gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was defeated he was in Zhou Di's camp.

sentences.zh: 後依陳寶應，寶應平，方詣闕。

translations.literal: Later he relied on Chen Baoying; when Baoying was pacified he finally came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Later he relied on Chen Baoying; when Baoying was pacified he finally came to court.

sentences.zh: 曆侍中，中書令，都官尚書。

translations.literal: He successively held Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰光子。

translations.literal: When he died his posthumous title was Guangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his posthumous title was Guangzi.

sentences.zh: 有文集行於世。

translations.literal: Collected works circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 子儼位侍中、御史中丞、太常卿；

translations.literal: His son Yan held the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary, Imperial Censor, and Grand Master of Ceremonies;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan held Attendant-in-Ordinary, Imperial Censor, and Grand Master of Ceremonies;

sentences.zh: 瀹位尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Yue held the post of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yue held Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 舉兄子僑字國美。

translations.literal: Ju's elder brother's son Qiao, styled Guomei.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's elder brother's son Qiao, courtesy name Guomei.

sentences.zh: 父玄大，仕梁侍中。

translations.literal: His father Xuan Da served Liang as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan Da served Liang as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 僑素貴，嘗一朝無食，其子啟欲以班史質錢，答曰：「寧餓死，豈可以此充食乎？

translations.literal: Qiao by nature was noble; once he had no food all morning; his son suggested pawning the Han History for money; he replied, "Better to starve—how can one use this to fill the belly?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was noble by nature; once he had no food all morning; his son suggested pawning the Han History for money; he replied, "Better to starve than use this to fill the belly."

sentences.zh: 」太清元年卒，集十卷。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Taiqing; collected works ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taiqing one; his collected works ran ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 長子褘。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Hui.

sentences.zh: 僑弟劄字世高，亦博涉文史，位湘東王諮議，先僑卒。

translations.literal: Qiao's younger brother Zha, styled Shigao, also broadly mastered literature and history and held the post of Adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong; he died before Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's younger brother Zha, courtesy name Shigao, also broadly mastered literature and history and was Adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong; he died before Qiao.

sentences.zh: 論曰：易雲，「積善之家，必有餘慶。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Changes says, "The house that accumulates good deeds will have surplus blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: The Changes says, "The house that accumulates good deeds will have surplus blessing."

sentences.zh: 」弘微立履所蹈，人倫播美，其世濟不隕，蓋有馮焉。

translations.literal: Hongwei in standing and treading spread beauty through human relations; his line for generations did not fall—surely there was support in this.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwei in conduct spread beauty through human relations; his line for generations did not fall—surely there was support in this.

sentences.zh: 敬沖出入三代，驟經遷革，遁俗之志，無聞貞固之道，居官之方，未免貨財之累。

translations.literal: Jingchong passed through three ages and suddenly met repeated changes; his will to escape the vulgar was heard, but his steadfast way was not; in the method of holding office he could not avoid the burden of seeking wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong passed through three dynasties and met repeated upheavals; his wish to escape the vulgar was known, but steadfast integrity was not; in holding office he could not avoid the taint of seeking wealth.

sentences.zh: 因傴成敬，偃仰當年。

translations.literal: Bending the body to achieve respect, bowing and rising in that age.
translations.idiomatic: Bending the body to win respect, bowing and rising through that age.

sentences.zh: 古人云：處士全盜虛聲，斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: The ancients said: The recluse wholly steals empty fame—this fits the saying.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: The recluse wholly steals empty fame—this is the man they meant.
